newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Seven killed in fresh violence in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Seven killed in fresh violence in Pakistan.

text.p: Seven people were killed overnight, five of them in Karachi, amid simmering ethnic and religious violence in Pakistan, police said on Thursday.

Police in this southern port city said masked gunmen ambushed a passenger bus in the industrial Korangi area of District East, killing a young man sitting on the roof and another inside. There was no claim of responsibility.
They said a 25-year-old man, identified only as Usman, was shot dead in the Landhi area of District East, while two bodies stuffed into sacks were found in Districts West and East.

The official APP news agency said an income tax official named Mobeen Malik and his wife had been shot dead by gunmen after a car chase on Wednesday night while they were travelling from Gujranwala to the Punjab provincial capital of Lahore.
Two children of Malik's brother were wounded in the attack, for which the motive was not immediately clear. The killing of Malik and his wife brought Wednesday's toll to 16 dead and 34 wounded.
Violence has surged in Pakistan in recent weeks as militant Sunni and Shi'ite Moslems wage a vendetta in Punjab and rival wings of an ethnic party feud in Karachi.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif hinted after a cabinet meeting that the federal government might intervene if the provincial governments failed to control security.

Sharif told the cabinet that "while he had the greatest respect for the autonomy of the provinces as provided under the constitution, the federal government could not remain indefinitely indifferent to the situation", a statement said.
The prime minister told the Interior Ministry to set up a round-the-clock control room to monitor the situation.

The meeting in Islamabad coincided with fresh sectarian attacks in which gunmen attacked a Sunni mosque in Lahore, killing at least six worshippers and wounding two, hours after a Shi'ite had been shot dead in a city bazaar.
A bomb hurled at a Sunni mosque in the Punjab city of Multan killed three men and wounded about 30.
Twelve people, most of them Shi'ites, were killed in three shooting attacks in Punjab province on Monday.

Officials say more than 130 people, including religious scholars, lawyers and doctors, have been killed in Sunni-Shi'ite violence this year. Shi'ites form about 15 percent of Pakistan's mainly Sunni population of more than 135 million.
More than 225 people have died in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi this year, compared to about 500 last year and more than 2,000 in 1995.
